title: The Last Visitor
premise: Elodie Fairweather is hired to appraise Fairweather House, the estate her estranged grandmother left her, and discovers the property's inventory keeps changing: rooms that weren't there yesterday, photographs where an extra chair appears beside the family. The house is counting its inhabitants, preparing to keep them, and the frost creeping up the windows is writing the final tally. Elodie, who grew up invisible in a family that never claimed them, realizes the house offers belonging at the price of selfhood, and that their grandmother chose to stay rather than be counted. In the end, Elodie gathers the scattered Fairweathers, gets them out before the first hard frost completes the count, and burns the deed, choosing found family over inheritance, while the house stands empty, still counting.
about_author: Ada Vane spent a decade as a building inspector before turning to horror, and her stories are obsessed with the ways houses remember. She writes from a rented cottage she refuses to buy, on principle.

chapters.title: The Inventory
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Arriving at Fairweather House to appraise their inheritance, Elodie finds it immaculate, warm, and waiting, though the grandmother has been dead for months. A survey reveals a room not on any blueprint, and in the family photographs, a chair has appeared beside every gathering. Emotional beat: wary curiosity curdling into the recognition of being watched.

chapters.title: The Count
chapters.summary: Alternating Elodie and cousin Marisol's POV. The Fairweathers convene to discuss the sale, and the house begins accommodating them: beds made, doors that open onto rooms from childhood. Elodie counts eleven doors at night and twelve by morning. Emotional beat: seduction, the house offering the belonging their family never did.

chapters.title: The Frost Writes
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV, then Elodie's. The frost patterns on the windows resolve into tally marks, one per family member, and the youngest cousin nearly vanishes into the blueprint room. Elodie finds grandmother's journal: she stayed, and was counted. Emotional beat: terror and grief braided together as the deadline, first frost, becomes visible.

chapters.title: What the House Cannot Hold
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. On the eve of the frost, Elodie refuses the house's final offer, a room made perfectly in their image, and leads the family out, burning the deed in the hearth as the count reaches its last mark. The house stands empty, windows dark, still counting. Emotional beat: costly release; Elodie chooses people over place, and is finally, freely seen.
